prompt: Benjamin Waterhouse Hawkins was commissioned to sculpt a series of life-size dinosaurs between 1852-54.  In this location, one species only had its head and back built with the rest of its body submerged underwater because they didn't know what it looked like then.  Where is this display located in 2024, which dinosaur species was this, and what did the rest of its body look like after all?
answer:
In 2024, the display was still in **Crystal Palace Park, Sydenham, south London**, partly submerged in one of the park’s lakes.

The animal was **Mosasaurus**—technically a giant prehistoric marine lizard, not a dinosaur. Benjamin Waterhouse Hawkins built only its **head, neck, part of the back and a flipper**, leaving the remainder underwater because only the skull and a few other bones were known at the time.

The rest of the sculpture was never completed or revealed. Modern fossil evidence shows that Mosasaurus had a **long, streamlined, lizard-like body, four paddle-shaped limbs and a powerful elongated tail**, rather like a huge marine monitor lizard.
